column1: # CHARLOTTE LEIBHOLZ, AND SHE IS NOT IN THE BOROUGH SHE LIVED IN.
# Landesarchiv Berlin, Standesamt Tempelhof, P Rep. 150 Nr. 943, Namensverzeichnis zum Sterberegister 1982,
# page 76. Found 8 October 2026 in the West Berlin sweep. Confirmed at the image.
# WHY THIS FILE IS SEPARATE FROM THE SWEEP IT CAME OUT OF. The sweep is fifty-one offices' worth of
# negatives with four incidental names in it. THIS IS NOT INCIDENTAL. It is the first LEIBHOLZ death
# this archive has found in any Berlin register except Günther's in 1939, and the forename is one of the
# four this archive has been looking for by name since September.
field
*** LEIBHOLZ geb. SCHÖTZOW · CHARLOTTE HERTA MARIE · 14. 1. · 161 · ev. ***
column2: STERBEREGISTER TEMPELHOF 1982 NR. 161, died 14 JANUARY 1982, evangelisch. The page is TYPEWRITTEN, not script, and the entry sits between LEHRKE, Margarete Erna and LEIFER geb. Asmus — the exact alphabetical slot. Crop at site/public/leibholz-tempelhof-1982.png.

column1: and "geb. Schötzow" settles something the archive never knew
column2: LEIBHOLZ WAS HER MARRIED NAME AND SCHÖTZOW HER BIRTH NAME. This archive has never established, for any of the four women it is hunting, whether Leibholz was the name they were born with or the name they married into. For this one it is now on a document.

column1: *** AND THE TEXT LAYER NEARLY LOST HER. ***
column2: the OCR of that line reads "Lehrke Margarete Erna 26. 7.| 1521 eV. Bnnn W LEibhOo1z" — HER SURNAME WAS SWEPT ONTO THE END OF THE ROW ABOVE AND MANGLED, and her own row came through with no surname at all. A scan matching the literal string LEIBHOLZ would have missed her. She was caught only because the pattern is Le[iy][bp]h and because a garbled token in the right alphabetical place was opened rather than filtered out as noise.

column1: # ---------------- IS SHE CHARLOTTE OF THE HASENHEIDE ----------------
WHAT THE ARCHIVE HOLDS ABOUT THAT WOMAN, IN FULL
column2: one line, from the post-war Berlin directory sweep: "LEIBHOLZ CHARLOTTE, HASENHEIDE, 1957 TO 1967". No forenames beyond Charlotte, no house number, no birth date, no maiden name, no trade. She is carried in lines.json among the UNPLACED Leibholz of Berlin.

column1: WHY SHE IS A STRONG CANDIDATE
column2: THE SURNAME IS LEIBHOLZ IN THE SAME SPELLING, the forename matches, and the geography is right: the HASENHEIDE IS IN NEUKÖLLN AND TEMPELHOF IS THE NEXT BOROUGH. *** AND NEUKÖLLN IS NOW EXHAUSTED: *** all twelve of its death-index volumes 1967-1992 were read on 7 October, two of them at the image, and there is no Leibholz and no Leipholz in any of them. A woman who leaves a Neukölln directory in 1967 and is not in Neukölln's registers for the next twenty-six years has to have died somewhere, and the borough next door is the first place to look.

column1: *** WHY SHE IS NOT CLAIMED, AND THIS IS NOT A FORMALITY ***
column2: CHARLOTTE WAS ONE OF THE COMMONEST GERMAN FORENAMES OF THAT GENERATION. "Geb. Schötzow" is a maiden name this archive has never held and cannot check against anything. Nothing joins the directory line to the register entry except a surname, a forename and two adjacent boroughs — and this archive has published a wrong identification built on exactly that much before, with the Bloom mariner.

column1: WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, AND IT IS ONE DOCUMENT
column2: a 1982 German death entry carries the BIRTH DATE, the BIRTHPLACE, the LAST ADDRESS, the MARITAL STATUS and the informant. IF THE ADDRESS IS THE HASENHEIDE, OR ANYWHERE IN NEUKÖLLN, THE QUESTION CLOSES. Standesamt Tempelhof, Sterberegister 1982 Nr. 161, orderable by number through service.berlin.de. *** THAT IS A PURCHASE AND DAVID'S TO MAKE. ***

column1: *** THE FREE TEST WAS RUN THE SAME HOUR, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT IT CANNOT BE RUN AT ALL. ***
column2: All seven post-war Namenteil volumes holding the surname and ALL TEN TELEPHONE BOOKS from 1969-70 to 1980-81 were opened at the Leibholz block. *** CHARLOTTE IS IN NO TELEPHONE BOOK, IN ANY YEAR. *** The Leibholz entries across the whole telephone run are FELIX (to 1970-71), AGNES at Mehringdamm 109, HILDE at Wiesbadener Str. 57 and ERNA at Streitstr. 39 — and never Charlotte. SHE NEVER HAD A TELEPHONE IN HER OWN NAME, so the instrument that bounded Agnes to 1979-80 and Friedrich to 1973-74 CAN NEVER PLACE HER. That is not a negative about the woman; it is a negative about the method, and it means the certificate is not one route among several but the only one.

column1: AND THE SAME PASS SHARPENED HER OWN DATES AND GAVE THE ARCHIVE A HOUSE NUMBER IT DID NOT HAVE
column2: *** LEIBHOLZ CHARLOTTE, NEUKÖLLN, HASENHEIDE 61-62 *** — present in the Namenteil of 1957, 1959, 1961, 1963, 1964 and 1967, and ABSENT FROM 1970, which is the first time the far end has been read rather than assumed. The archive's line was "Hasenheide, 1957 to 1967" with no number. In 1963 she is in the STREET section at that house among Kühn, Lipp, Mattner, Mühlniel, Pommerenke, Rotter, Schmale, Schule and Thaeter. A neighbour of hers, PAUL LEIBICH, OFENSETZER, lived at HASENHEIDE 92 in the same years — a stove-fitter two hundred metres away, and this archive has spent weeks on JOACHIM LUWINSKI, OFENSETZER. COINCIDENCE OF TRADE AND STREET, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A CONNECTION.

column1: and one free test that can be run first
column2: the post-war Berlin directories and telephone books run to 1980-81 and have been swept for this surname. CHARLOTTE IS RECORDED AS PRESENT 1957-1967 AND THE LAST LEIBHOLZ IN THE WHOLE RUN IS HILDE of Wiesbadener Straße 57 in 1980-81. If Charlotte reappears in any volume after 1967 at a TEMPELHOF address, that joins the two women without paying for anything. The slot has not been read year by year for her the way it was for Agnes and Friedrich.

column1: # ---------------- WHAT IT DOES TO THE SWEEP'S OWN PREMISE ----------------
*** THE WHOLE POINT OF GOING BOROUGH BY BOROUGH IS NOW DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ARGUED ***
column2: the archivist's letter of 29 September says there are 150+ Standesämter and NO NAME INDEX ACROSS THEM, which is why "she moved to another borough" has been an unanswerable shrug in four work list rows. THE FIRST LEIBHOLZ THIS SWEEP FOUND WAS IN A BOROUGH NOBODY HAD A REASON TO OPEN. Tempelhof was on the list because it is one of the twelve West Berlin boroughs, not because anyone connected it to anybody.
